title: Ordinary module pullback oplax mate on balanced generators
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and take their small pro-étale sites small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also writing $R_T$ for its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary module operations, their specified adjunctions, and geometric composition comparisons of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Use relative tensors [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] internally and sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] externally, identified by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Give internal pullback its actual oplax structure induced by the abelian inverse-image mate structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and extension of scalars [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. For all internal $R_Y$-module objects $M,N$, under $E_X,E_Y$ the ordinary oplax tensor arrow is the normalized ringed comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. Writing $S=R_X$, $R'=f^{-1}R_Y$, it sends $s\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$ from $S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}(M\otimes_{R_Y}N)$ to $(S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}M)\otimes_S(S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}N)$. Its inverse sends $(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)$ to $st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. The unit comparison is scalar multiplication, and these formulas respect the associators and unitors.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; comparison with the specified module-object oplax mate

proof.text: Write $L=f^*_{\rm sec}$, $P=f_{*,\rm sec}$, and let $\Phi$ be their specified Hom bijection. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E_X,E_Y$ identify the relative tensor, regular unit and constraints by the identity on local pure tensors. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], they identify the internal pull-push adjunction with $L\dashv P$, including unit and counit. The comparisons are exactly those fixed in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Thus $L(A)=S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}A$ and $P$ is geometric direct image with scalar restriction along $c:R_Y\to f_*S$. The internal adjunction is the composite of the transported abelian adjunction, whose unit is the geometric insertion, with extension and restriction of scalars [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. The extension adjunction [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] says its unit is insertion of $1$; consequently the module unit $u_A:A\to PLA$ is geometric insertion followed by $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. No alternative choice of adjunction is being made.

Identify the actual direct-image pairing before taking mates. The abelian direct image is restriction along $V\mapsto V\times_YX$. The generator equation [lem-sfb-sheaf-pushforward-generator-comparison] identifies its actual lax tensor map with the restriction of the sheaf pure-tensor pairing. In [def-sfb-module-lower-star], scalar restriction changes only the action. Compose this ambient pairing with the balancing projection defining relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For $a,b$ local sections and $r\in R_Y$, the images of $(ra)\otimes b$ and $a\otimes(rb)$ agree: both equal $c(r)(a\otimes b)$. Hence the pairing factors through the $R_Y$-balanced tensor, sending $a\otimes b$ to $a\otimes b$. Its unit sends $r$ to $c(r)$. The pure-tensor identifications of Step 1 therefore identify this internal pairing with the unique section-module lax structure of [lem-pd-ringed-direct-image-pairing-lax]. These statements concern maps out of the sheafified tensor, not preservation of tensor products by evaluation.

source.place: Tags 03D6, definition-pushforward; 03EK, section-tensor-product; ambient generator equation and balanced factorization

proof.text: Check that the stipulated internal oplax map is the mate of the pairing in Step 2. Write $F=f^*_{\rm Ab}$, $G=f_*^{\rm Ab}$ and $v$ for the abelian adjunction unit. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate], its actual ambient tensor map $d$ satisfies $G(d)\,v_{A\otimes B}=m_{FA,FB}(v_A\otimes v_B)$, with $m$ the actual lax map of $G$. Precompose with the relative-tensor balancing projection. Naturality of $v$ moves this projection through $v$, and the two action maps have equal images by the balance equation of Step 2; this gives the same mate equation for the induced relative-tensor map. For the extension-of-scalars part, [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] computes its transpose by precomposition with insertion $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Its tensor mate therefore sends the inserted pair to $(1\otimes a)\otimes(1\otimes b)$; scalar linearity determines its values with arbitrary leading scalar. The module adjunction is precisely the composite of these two Hom bijections [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Applying them successively to the stipulated composite oplax map consequently gives $m_{f^*M,f^*N}(u_M\otimes u_N)$. The same computation on the regular unit gives $c$. Thus both actual internal structure maps are the module adjunction mates of Step 2, not just isomorphisms with the correct endpoints.

proof.text: Use [lem-pd-monoidal-adjunction-equivalence-transport] with the strong monoidal equivalences of Step 1, its identified adjunctions, and the lax pairing identified in Step 2. Its hypotheses hold: the equivalences are fully faithful and essentially surjective, their constraints are the fixed pure-tensor constraints, and the right-adjoint comparison preserves both pairing and unit by Step 2. Step 3 then identifies the image of the actual internal oplax map with the specified section-adjunction mate. Apply [lem-pd-ringed-tensor-adjunction-mate] to this ringed geometric morphism. The sites have the required size, their rings are commutative, $P$ is precomposition with scalar restriction, its unit is $c$, and the module adjunction unit is geometric insertion followed by scalar insertion, as verified above. That lemma identifies this mate with the normalized canonical ringed tensor comparison, including its generalized pure-tensor equation. In particular its tensor map is $D:s\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$, and its unit is $D_0:s\otimes r\mapsto s\alpha_f(r)$.

proof.text: For clarity check the inverse formulas using balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $B((s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n))=st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. Moving $r\in R'$ across either inner tensor gives respectively $s\alpha_f(r)t\otimes(m\otimes n)=st\otimes(rm\otimes n)$ or $st\alpha_f(r)\otimes(m\otimes n)=st\otimes(m\otimes rn)$. Moving a scalar of $S$ between the outer factors gives the same product; commutativity of $S$ is used here. These equations and additivity make $B$ well-defined and compatible with restriction, so it sheafifies. Now $BD(s\otimes(m\otimes n))=s\otimes(m\otimes n)$, whereas $DB((s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n))=(st\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)=(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)$. The last equality is outer $S$-balancing. The unit inverse is $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, since $s\alpha_f(r)\otimes1=s\otimes r$. Tensor and sheafification universal properties extend these identities from their defining generators.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; scalar balancing and sheafification universal properties

proof.text: The constraints are the specified ones: [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies associators and both unitors with their ordinary balanced-tensor versions. After rebracketing, both paths in the oplax associativity diagram send $s\otimes(m\otimes n\otimes p)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)\otimes(1\otimes p)$. In the left-unit diagram both paths send $s\otimes(r\otimes m)$ to $s\alpha_f(r)\otimes m=s\otimes rm$; in the right-unit diagram they send $s\otimes(m\otimes r)$ to $s\alpha_f(r)\otimes m=s\otimes rm$. Additivity, balancing and the sheafification universal property give equality of the diagram maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. As $B=D^{-1}$ and $D_0^{-1}(s)=s\otimes1$, the inverse constraint diagrams follow by composing these equalities with the inverses. Hence the asserted formulas respect associators and unitors.
